conventions.convention: The score is the spatial gradient of the log of the specified density, defined only where that density is positive, finite and differentiable.
For state-dependent covariance a, probability-flow velocity is b − (div a)/2 − a score/2. The theorem assumes a global jointly C1 flow of diffeomorphisms and asserts equality of one-time marginals.
Reverse time increases as u = T − t. The reverse drift is −b + div a + a score, evaluated at forward time T − u.

The sampler assumes AC, uses 0 < ε < T and N ≥ 1, starts from the actual terminal law P_T, and returns a finite-step state at forward time ε. Each predictor precedes a corrector targeting the next forward-time density, with mutually independent standard Gaussian inputs.
N(0, θ) uses θ as variance; the VP schedule has continuous strictly positive β on a finite compact time interval.

load_bearing.statement: On the set of points x where 0 < p_t(x) < ∞ and the map x ↦ p_t(x) is differentiable, the marginal score of P_t is s_t(x) := ∇_x log p_t(x).

For positive classical probability densities satisfying the stated Fokker–Planck equation, assume the velocity v = b − (div a)/2 − a∇log p/2 has the specified global C1 flow of diffeomorphisms. For Z_0 with law P_0 and Z_t = Φ_{t,0}(Z_0), Z_t has law P_t for every t ∈ [0,T]; no equality of path laws is asserted.

Given the stated positive-density diffusion and reversal hypotheses, AC, 0 < ε < T, N ≥ 1 and positive corrector step sizes, initialize Y_0 ∼ P_T. At each of N time levels perform the displayed reverse Euler–Maruyama predictor and one unadjusted Langevin corrector using the next-time exact marginal score. Return Y_N at forward time ε.
